standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of a C_1 field: every homogeneous form of degree d in more than d variables has a nontrivial zero

standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces Br(K) = 0 to the statement that no finite dimensional division algebra with centre K of degree greater than one exists.

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of a central division algebra by the separable closure and the reduced norm
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the fact that D tensor_K K^sep is isomorphic to Mat_d(K^sep) uniquely up to inner isomorphism, so that the determinant descends
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the Galois invariant determinant, hence the homogeneous degree d reduced norm map N_red : D -> K used in the counted argument.

core_obligations: Reduce to division algebras (proof lines 10839-10840): let D be a finite dimensional division algebra over K with centre K, since Br(K) is generated by the classes of such algebras.

Obtain the reduced norm (proof lines 10841-10849): using that D tensor_K K^sep is isomorphic to Mat_d(K^sep) uniquely up to inner isomorphism, the determinant on Mat_d(K^sep) is Galois invariant and descends to a homogeneous degree d map N_red : D -> K.

Apply the C1 property (proof lines 10850-10852): if d > 1, the homogeneous degree d form N_red on D, whose dimension over K is d^2 > d, has a nonzero zero, so there is a nonzero x in D with N_red(x) = 0.
Conclude (proof lines 10851-10852): such an x is not invertible, contradicting that D is a division algebra; hence d = 1 and Br(K) = 0.
proof_roadmap: Let D be a finite dimensional division algebra over K with centre K.
Split by the separable closure to get D tensor K^sep isomorphic to Mat_d(K^sep) up to inner isomorphism.
Descend the determinant to the reduced norm N_red : D -> K, a homogeneous form of degree d on a d^2-dimensional space.
If d > 1, the C1 property gives a nonzero x with N_red(x) = 0, and such an x is a non-invertible element of D, a contradiction.
difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the Brauer group of a C1 field as zero (statement lines 10833-10836). The argument passes through an explicit construction: a finite dimensional central division algebra D over K of degree d is split by the separable closure, D tensor_K K^sep being isomorphic to Mat_d(K^sep) uniquely up to inner isomorphism, so the determinant is Galois invariant and descends to the reduced norm N_red : D -> K, a homogeneous form of degree d on the d^2-dimensional K-space D (proof lines 10841-10849). The non-formal point is the C1 input: for d > 1 the form has more variables than its degree, so it has a nonzero zero, and a nonzero element with vanishing reduced norm is not invertible, contradicting divisionality (proof lines 10850-10852). The claim is H2: one descent construction and one application of the C1 hypothesis.
